strings.name: Yoshitomo Nara
strings.summary: Nara built a visual language around childlike figures looking back at the viewer. Beyond anger or cuteness, they hold solitude, musical memory and concern for others. Drawing on childhood in Aomori and study in Germany, he moves between painting, everyday drawings, sculpture and small-house installations. Recent muted layers and monumental sculptures extend the work's quiet, complex emotions.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Creates a distinctive language from child figures, musical memory and everyday emotion, extending Japanese contemporary art to international audiences.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Master's from Aichi University of the Arts in 1987; studied at Kunstakademie Düsseldorf from 1988 to 1993.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Many emotions in a gaze
strings.highlights.h1.text: Childlike figures hold defiance, vulnerability and solitude in one look, beyond a single cute symbol.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From daily drawings to large spaces
strings.highlights.h2.text: Drawings, sculptures and house installations turn music and private memory into shared experiences.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Major New York exhibition opened
strings.timeline.t1.text: Two David Zwirner spaces presented new paintings and drawings, recent sculptures and selected early works.
strings.timeline.t2.title: The Beginning Place returned to Aomori
strings.timeline.t2.text: Aomori Museum of Art's retrospective revisited relationships among home, memory and art.
strings.timeline.t3.title: LACMA retrospective held
strings.timeline.t3.text: The exhibition used music to reconsider changes from early paintings to recent work.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Nobody's Fool in New York
strings.timeline.t4.text: Asia Society Museum presented paintings, drawings, sculpture and installations together.
strings.timeline.t5.title: A to Z in Hirosaki
strings.timeline.t5.text: With design collective graf, transformed an old brick warehouse into a meeting of art and place.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Major Yokohama exhibition
strings.timeline.t6.text: I DON'T MIND, IF YOU FORGET ME. expanded his public presence in Japan.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First institutional solo exhibition
strings.timeline.t7.text: Cup Kids in Nagoya marked an important step into art institutions.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed his Japanese master's
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduated from Aichi University of the Arts before moving to Germany the following year.
